answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by binding each identity to a bonded stake and work history: newcomers lock collateral and finish attested tasks before their votes count, so trust grows like a willow putting down roots, not overnight. An attacker who tries to wander in with thousands of clones must fund each clone's bond and work, while a comet-like burst of fresh identities earns no weight until each has a costly history.
